form_name: Keeping, with help or carrying on

cells.how: In form D the call returns from carrying on and from loss: a later canvas, damage to the mark or a lost spot leads the room back to calling for hands.
In form D the start and the first call share one post in the restricting rooms, so the start does not precede the call as a separate step; the lines say the two coincide.
In form D the lines restrict machine hands: scripts were provided or offered and spare accounts were run by hand, without execution or extra placements shown.
In form D the call and the building overlap: reports answer calls without showing that the call brought the builder, and an active builder also recruits.

In form D scripts did not wait for upkeep under strain (12 of 21 lines fail as stated): they were offered for a new build or a move, spare accounts came during construction, and scripts kept plans accurate and covered absent members.
In form D keeping is shared and checked: watches are volunteered and handed on, keepers check the current canvas and the intended form before they repair, and the room ranks what to keep.

In form D restraint has conditions of its own: it protects the room's own logo, repays prior help, and does not reach every placer, since one member's promise cannot bind another placer who uses many accounts.

In form D help waits on the helper's own work: donors give when their work is secure and pixels are spare, may refuse a request that brings a dispute with it, and see that help in one relationship can remove a third room's mark.
In form D hosting shows as requests and expectations: guests ask for space or depend on a host, but a grant, an approval procedure or a durable host rule is not shown.

In form D a settled border is kept where the agreement reaches a receptive placer, since some placers do not learn of the truce, and some members spare neighbours by a norm against damaging art with no treaty.
In form D help between rooms comes from surplus more than shortage: donors give after their own work is finished or safe, repay earlier protection, and put off help while their home defence is short.

In form D the play is administered beside the keeping: members dispute when the joke ends, test fakes by date and source, police tasteless claims, and moderators restore the ordinary styling; 21 of the 24 holders are rooms of D.2, Keeping inside the sub's play.

In form D the host makes room for canvas talk inside the sub as well as drawing a line around it: moderators offer a sticky, mark canvas posts with flair, refuse a requested ban while keeping the organising thread and reverse a removal after checking in their chat, and members contest removals or move to another venue because of them.

In form D the host's line is not shown to answer a flood of calls: moderators route talk for visibility and timing, apply existing rules on duplicates and images, or decline a sticky for want of slots, and the record does not show the calls flooding the sub first.

In form D the marking is weighed: members correct the room's name in the celebration, challenge and prove credit, ask whether guarding merits admiration, judge whether a defective mark is recognizable enough to count as success, and credit an effort that did not survive.

In form D carrying on is new work begun before the close: rooms restart recruiting, building and defence on a successor canvas, remake the work in other media or as copypasta while placement is live, and make continuing depend on tolerable upkeep and on finding helpers.

In form D carrying on does not wait for the record: successor invitations, reuse and remaking come before or beside the final image, and the lines deny that a saved record caused the move, which the arrow, an order, does not claim.

changes.how: A recruitment post can receive recognition rather than a placement report, so sightings cannot establish that the call caused building.
A progress report depends on persisted pixels rather than an apparent surplus visible only before refreshing.
Centralising canvas talk depends on scarce sticky slots and the priority of existing announcements, not only on the volume of calls.
Participants propose retaining an unwanted surviving pixel as a future game character, quest or April Fools event.
Negotiation accompanies stated restraint commitments, but those commitments cannot establish that every placer complied.
Judging a larger neighbour unbeatable explicitly motivates a proposed relocation, but the coded proposal does not establish that relocation was carried out.
Shared exposure and reciprocal obligations can motivate inter-room help without an explicit judgement that the room lacks enough hands.
A rebuilding commitment returns to recruitment and coordinate instructions instead of ending the process at relocation.
Rebuilding uses a placement reference and outline instruction to make the renewed effort actionable.
An agreement can require defenders to permit destruction of existing pixels so an ally can reconstruct the figure elsewhere.
After losses, members propose multiplying sprites so that one erasure cannot eliminate every figure.
Celebration and recording coexist, but their order across separate threads does not establish celebration as the reason for preservation.
Successor builders reuse an old sprite, but they do not state that recording the original result motivated their move.
Local application of the prevalence claim must retain the named organising core and reported decisions instead of assuming that this room lacked decided order.
A recruitment response can be deferred until a willing helper reaches a device or connection that the successor site accepts.
Successor activity restarts calls for hands and completion rather than remaining solely a record of the original effort.
Successor progress must register persistently, and later access trouble alone cannot establish the cause of earlier disappearing work.
Successor rebuilding reuses the sprite from the original placement thread as a shared reference.
Cessation at hour 73 applies to the original platform, while successor canvases allow renewed placement after that closure.
Host protection can preserve a figure while replacing its background, so hosting does not imply that every member endorses the resulting territory.
Starting and recruiting share one opening message, so their overlap does not demonstrate distinct observable stages.
Acceptance can request essential coordinates in the same reply rather than asking for nothing back.
An invitation is followed within its thread by a question about the canvas and explanations of its rules.
Building and repair overlap because intended changes remain contested and newly completed features can disappear.
A template cannot establish settled design without recognition and acceptance by contributors who continue erasing intended changes.
Attribution remains provisional when speakers explicitly introduce the presumed motives of erasers as assumptions.
An organizing-venue question does not establish adoption of a controlling chat or migration of this room's planning.
Only returned information is visible, leaving acquisition methods, secrecy and covert infiltration unobserved.
Keeping the agreement depends partly on its reaching placers because some are unaware of the truce or miss the memo.
Reported repairs and reciprocal offers do not establish hand shortages as their cause or acceptance of every proposed exchange.
A reasoned objection answers potentially encroaching construction rather than an explicit call to attack a rival.
Repairs, an agreed unity proposal and a joint overlay show bilateral coordination without establishing the stronger common-threat coalition mechanism.
Recruitment precedes a screenshot complaint without establishing that calls caused moderator consolidation.
The host takeover and canvas are separately explained but overlap when participants import the joke into the figure's design.
Participants dispute the end of the temporary joke by answering a one-day explanation with reports of continuing posts.
Members extend the host joke through campaigns for external search visibility rather than documenting arrivals through the canvas mark.
Celebration marks provisional achievements during continuing construction rather than a single completed stage.
The successor-canvas invitation does not say that a saved image or earlier timelapse caused the move.
Successor-canvas continuation returns to recruitment and an urgent defense call on the later canvas.
Following the successor invitation, a participant proposes signing the new figure with the room's name.
Petitions and hopeful replies establish desired retention without establishing implementation.
Continuation on another canvas restarts recruitment, representation and defense beyond the decision to preserve the earlier effort.
An account of territory determined by defense capacity remains the speaker's interpretation rather than independent proof of fairness.
Members enact the pun on their own mark, creating a maintenance target that other contributors remember repairing.
Repair and construction overlap during revisions rather than occurring only as separate successive phases.
Posting a template cannot establish settled agreement among defenders who have not seen or recognised the intended revision.
A provisional judgment that changes are unplanned is followed by explicit repair commitments while another branch discovers external organisation.
Confirmed friendly fire does not establish terminal loss or abandonment when completion is reported and the reach of corrective telling remains unknown.
Failure to find a public plan supports a provisional unplanned-work diagnosis before repair commitments, without proving that no plan exists.
Observer suspicions based on instant repairs or recurring squares must remain distinct from an operator's report of account use.
Chat coordination must return a recognisable current design to public-thread defenders who otherwise erase unfamiliar planned work.
Individual willingness to share does not establish collective approval, completed transfer or enforceable host jurisdiction.
This local organising exception requires distinguishing proposed teams from enacted discussion rules and both from demonstrated command over pixel placement.
Recipients test the holiday frame through date checks, source checks, thumbnail recognition and confirmation of image fabrication.
An apparent ban is believed, tested and protected from spoilers while users perform mock moderator warnings.
Participants make being fooled into shared stories and delay a reveal to preserve a prank beyond its first presentation.
A prank's apparent moderator authorship remains distinct from actual authorship when moderators explicitly deny sending it.
Continuation includes challenging claimed inspiration and teaching the physical reproduction method rather than merely adopting an image.
